references.text: God calls Abraham by name ('Abraham! Abraham!') and Abraham answers, 'Here I am' – exactly the same pattern of double naming and response as in Gen 46:2.
God speaks to Jacob in a dream at Bethel, an earlier example of God communicating with him through nighttime visions.
God commands Jacob to go up to Bethel, showing a pattern of God's direct guidance in Jacob's life.
God calls Moses by name ('Moses! Moses!') and Moses answers, 'Here I am' – the same pattern of double naming and הִנֵּנִי response.
God calls Samuel by name repeatedly, and Samuel answers, 'Here I am' – a similar calling pattern.
God communicates with prophets through visions (מראות), relevant to the expression 'visions at night' in the source verse.
The repetition of the name and the response 'Here I am' in a nighttime vision marks a direct parallel in God's way of revealing himself to the patriarchs.
The identical call-response structure ('Name! Name!' -> 'Here I am') shows a recurring pattern in God's encounters with the patriarchs.
It shares the central pattern of God's calling and the immediate response 'Here I am', even though the repetition of the name is missing.
